chapter: Later tours, illness and the union job
title: How hard the trumpet is and how to practice coming back
summary: He says the trumpet is the hardest instrument and describes returning with a few minutes of playing at a time.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Well after all, the trumpet is one of the hardest instruments.....
It sure is. I wish I kept playing the piano. The only thing about a piano is that you might get arthritis or something.

But most people don't. Most people, most piano players don't get it. But I didn't know the trumpet was the hardest. Sometimes when you pick it up if you're not feeling well it feels like it weighs two hundred pounds. And you've got to pick it up there and hold it and hold it just right so that the vibrato.

comes out. And it's got to be held a certain way. And sometimes you just, you just want to hold it down like this. Let it rest instead of ...... Sometimes you don't even want to pick it up. A lot of times. But I really don't complain about it.
Well when you, when you, when it you start back on xxxxxx, will it be a matter of practice at a little bit at a time?

Yes, very little. Very little. A little bit, put it down. You don't practice like you did when you practiced two or three hours. Even when you practiced two or three hours you're supposed to practice just maybe thirty minutes, forty minutes. Put it down for twenty and come back. Or even just for half an hour and lay off for half an hour until you get in two or three hours a day like that which takes all day.

But when you're coming back you do three or four minutes and put it down for ten minutes and then come back and just act like you're playing with it really to see if I can make a note. Make it and get away from it.
